newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ leads Prague bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ leads Prague bourse higher.

text.p: Late gains in shares of power company CEZ pushed the Prague Stock Exchange PX50 index up 1.2 points to a 1996 high of 582.0 points on Thursday after a dip at the morning price fixing.
The Reuters RPIX index measuring the seven blue chip stocks in realtime trading gained six points to close at 1,177.
High cap CEZ grew 20 crowns in the realtime session, after falling one crown in the morning, on low turnover of 3.3 million crowns.
But the gain pushed the indices up, with the help of Komercni Banka which closed five crowns higher at 2,455.
Overall on the market, just over one million shares changed hands on turnover of 728.4 million crowns.
Gainers outnumbered losers 299 to 253, and 178 issues held staedy at Wednesday's levels.
Insurance company Ceska Pojistovna lost 200 crowns to 3,800 prior to the company's announcement that it might post a loss this year.
Brokers said Pojistovna, which revealed on Thusrday that it expected zero result for this year due to loses from its failed bank Kreditini banka, was overpriced at its current level.
Pojistovna's general meeting approved a rights issue at 5,000 crowns per share.

The day's largest gain, 303 crown rise of the glas-fibre maker Vertex to 6,374, came as a surprise to analysts who have expected a long-term decline after the company's shares were the subject of a battle.
Pivovar Radegast, 20 percnet owned by Britain's Bass plc, gained 150 crowns to close at 4,150.
